content:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m writing to apply for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role at Corvale Mobility. I’m a QA automation engineer with seven years of experience, including the last two focused on CI/CD, test environments and build tooling, and I’m looking to move into DevOps and platform engineering. The opportunity to help shape infrastructure connecting a new train fleet with cloud services is a compelling next step for me.

At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and around 25 developers, from build and test stages through artifact publishing. By parallelising jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand ephemeral environments, I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes. I also built merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm charts on a shared Kubernetes cluster. These responsibilities have given me practical experience improving the reliability and day-to-day operation of shared infrastructure, while working across teams.

I bring hands-on experience with Linux, Docker, Helm, basic Kubernetes, Python and Bash, as well as a systems-oriented foundation in computer engineering. I’m particularly interested in Corvale’s end-to-end approach to ownership and the chance to contribute to a platform where reliability, observability and secure connectivity matter. My background is strongest in CI/CD and test infrastructure, and I would bring that experience and analytical approach to the team’s infrastructure and system-design work.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity platform.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately concise. It uses credible evidence from the CV, including ownership of GitLab CI pipelines, support for three product teams, pipeline-time reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, and Docker/Helm/Kubernetes test environments. The tone is honest about the candidate’s strongest experience and avoids claiming unsupported Terraform, AWS, networking, or security expertise. The main content weakness is that the letter presents relevant QA/test infrastructure experience but does not sufficiently connect the quantified reliability improvement and cross-team ownership to Corvale’s requirements for reliable, observable infrastructure.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard text, conventional headings are not required for a short letter, and there are no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It includes supported keywords such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Linux, Python, Bash, reliability, and infrastructure. However, AI/ATS screening probability for this specific role is likely moderate to low because the ad’s strongest screening terms—Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, systems architecture, system design, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and security—are absent. These cannot be added because they are not supported by the candidate information. The phrase “cloud services” appears in the company context, but the letter does not establish hands-on cloud infrastructure experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role’s infrastructure reliability, CI/CD, Linux, containerisation, Kubernetes, analytical, and cross-team collaboration themes. It also fits Corvale’s engineering-led culture through its emphasis on ownership, shared infrastructure, reliability, and working across teams. However, the candidate’s material indicates substantial gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, AWS or another major cloud platform, systems architecture/system design, networking including mTLS and SSL/TLS, practical security awareness, and train/IoT/remote-device integration. The material also does not establish virtual-machine experience or backend/full-stack development beyond Java test code. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting. The letter is strongest when positioning the candidate as an experienced test-infrastructure engineer transitioning toward DevOps, but that positioning is a weaker match than the role’s expected cloud infrastructure ownership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the second paragraph, make the reliability outcome more directly relevant to Corvale’s “observable, reliable and secure” platform by adding the supported flaky-test result after the pipeline-time result. For example, change the end of the paragraph to: “I also maintain an approximately 900-test pytest and Playwright suite and reduced its flaky-test rate from 7% to under 1%, giving me practical experience improving both delivery speed and test reliability.” Do not imply production-platform reliability beyond what the CV supports.
2. In the second paragraph, make the cross-team scope more explicit because the role requires leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along. Revise the final sentence to: “Owning this shared infrastructure for three product teams and approximately 25 developers has required coordinating changes across teams and making practical improvements that support developers’ day-to-day work.” This accurately strengthens the existing evidence without claiming formal leadership or stakeholder-management experience.
3. In the third paragraph, replace the broad phrase “systems-oriented foundation in computer engineering” with a more concrete, ATS-readable description grounded in the CV. For example: “I also bring a BEng in Computer Engineering and hands-on experience with Linux, containerised test environments, CI/CD automation, Python, Bash, PostgreSQL and basic Kubernetes.” This is more specific and avoids implying demonstrated systems-architecture experience that the candidate information does not establish.
4. In the third paragraph, change “the team’s infrastructure and system-design work” because it may suggest stronger system-design experience than the CV supports. Use a truthful transition-oriented formulation such as: “I would bring this CI/CD and test-infrastructure experience, together with an analytical approach, to the team’s infrastructure work while continuing to develop in cloud platform and system design.”

MINOR ENHANCEMENT
5. In the opening paragraph, retain the career-transition statement but connect it more directly to the role’s ownership theme. For example, change “I’m looking to move into DevOps and platform engineering” to “I’m now seeking to apply this infrastructure and automation experience in a broader DevOps or platform-engineering role.” This sounds more contribution-focused while remaining truthful.
